name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:mocks → /spec:plan → /spec:run (build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.218.0 — merge-back cleanup deletes a squash-merged branch even after the target has moved on: containment is proven by the merge changing nothing, not only by identical trees, so a squash close reaches DONE after the ledger commit lands on main; a merge retry after a landed squash now resumes at cleanup instead of re-running the merge against a dirty root. 7.217.0 — Genesis BRIEF stops ratifying prose (specs/20260930/01): --mark brief-written no longer writes or checks a one-page design doctrine or a design-rules manifest; conversational-bot and cli-devtool join the design-skipped archetypes; /spec:enforce, /spec:doctor, /spec:init and the grounding contract drop the design-rules manifest and its designRules hash key (contract hash changes: hosts re-stamp via /spec:doctor). 7.216.0 — A File Plan row on the new baseline layer names a file only the built product can produce and a person approves (a screenshot baseline): the build no longer demands it at TESTS or in a wave, and refuses the integrated mark until it exists, so the approval lands before the gate runs. The fleet evidence reader, run from inside a spec worktree, now scans the checkouts beside the main checkout instead of reporting zero repos.
